<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:state_existence}
  For every $u \in \hat U$ and $(f, y_0, y_1) \in L^2(I,H) \times V \times H$, there exists a unique (weak) solution $y = y(u) \in Z := C(\overline V) \cap C^1(\overline H)$ to \eqref{eq:wave-equation} satisfying
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:apriori}
    \| y \|_{C(\overline V)} + \| \partial_{t} y \|_{C(\overline H)} + \| \partial_{tt} y \|_{L^2({I}, V^*)} \le C_1(\| f \|_{L^2(I,H)} + \| y_0 \|_V + \| y_1 \|_H)
  \end{equation}
  for a constant $C_1$ independent of $(f,y_0, y_1) \in L^2(I,H) \times V \times H$ and $u \in \hat U$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:dual_existence}
  For every $u\in \hat U$ and $g\in L^2(I,H)$, $\varphi_0\in V$, and $\varphi_1 \in H$, there exists a unique solution $\varphi \in Z$ to \eqref{eq:dual} satisfying
  \begin{equation*}
    \| \varphi \|_{C(\overline I,V)} + \| \partial_t \varphi \|_{C(\overline I,H)}+\| \partial_{tt} \varphi \|_{L^2({I}, V^*)} \leq C_1 (\| g \|_{L^2(I,H)} + \| \varphi_0 \|_V + \| \varphi_1 \|_{H}).
  \end{equation*}
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:state_lipschitz}
  There exists a constant $L>0$ such that the mapping $u\mapsto y(u)$ satisfies
  \begin{equation*}
    \| y(u_1)-y(u_2) \|_{L^2(I,H)}\leq L \| u_1-u_2 \|_{L^\infty(\Omega)} \quad \text{for all }u_1,u_2\in \hat U.
  \end{equation*}
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:state_continuity}
  Let $\{u_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\subset \hat U$ be a sequence with $u_n\to u$ in $L^r(\Omega)$ for some $r\in [1,\infty)$. Then $u\in \hat U$ and $y(u_n)\rightharpoonup y(u)$ in $L^2(I,V)\cap W^{1,2}(I,H)\cap W^{2,2}(I,V^*)$. Furthermore, $y(u_n)\rightharpoonup y(u)$ in $H$ pointwise for all $t\in [0,T]$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:state_strong}
  Assume that $f\in L^2(I,V)$ and let $\{u_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\subset \hat U$ be a sequence with $u_n\to u$ in $L^\infty(\Omega)$. Then $y(u_n)\to y(u)$ in $L^2(I,V)\cap W^{1,2}(I,H)$.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- assumption-1: body_md -->
\label{ass:data} The data satisfy $f\in L^2(I;V)$ and $(y_0,y_1)\in H^2(\Omega)\times H^1(\Omega)$ with $\partial_\nu y_0 =0$. Furthermore,
  \begin{enumerate}
    \item $\hat u$ is constant on $\Omega\setminus \omega_c$ and
    \item $y_0$ is constant on $\omega_c$ and $\overline{\omega_c} \subset \Omega$.
  \end{enumerate}
<!-- end assumption-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:state_regularity}
  Let $u\in \hat U$ and \cref{ass:data} hold.
  Then there exists $q > 2$ and a constant $\hat C$ independent of $u$ such that $y(u) \in {L^\infty(I,W^{1,q}(\Omega))}$ and
  for all $u \in \hat U$,
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:state-regularity}
    \| y(u) \|_{L^\infty(I,W^{1,q}(\Omega))} \le \hat C\left(\| y_1 \|_{V} + \| y_0 \|_{H^2(\Omega)}+ \| f \|^2_{L^2(I,V)}\right).
  \end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
If \cref{ass:data} holds, the requirement in \cref{lem:state_strong} on the convergence of $u_n$ can be relaxed to $u_n\to u$ in $L^{\frac{q}{q-2}}(\Omega)$, where $q$ is the exponent from \cref{prop:state_regularity}. In this case, the first term on the right-hand side in \eqref{eq:state_strong1} can be estimated by Hölder's inequality as
  \begin{equation*}
    \int_{\Omega} |u_n-u| |\nabla y_n(t)|^2 \,\mathrm{d}x  \leq \| u_n-u \|_{L^{\frac{q}{q-2}}(\Omega)}\| y_n(t) \|_{L^\infty(I,W^{1,q}(\Omega))}^2\to 0,
  \end{equation*}
  where we used \cref{prop:state_regularity}. Then again $y(u_n) \to y(u)$ in $W$.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
In \cref{ass:data}\,(ii), the requirement $\overline {\omega_c} \subset \Omega$ was only used in Step 2 of the proof of \cref{prop:state_regularity}. It it is not necessary if instead $y_0\in H^3(\Omega)$ is assumed.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:existence:bv}
  For every $\varepsilon\geq 0$, there exists a global minimizer $\bar u\in BV(\omega_c)\cap U$ of $J_\varepsilon$.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:tracking_frechet}
  For every $\varepsilon>0$, the mapping $F_\varepsilon$ defined in \eqref{eq:tracking} is Fréchet differentiable in every $u\in L^\infty(\omega_c)$, and the Fréchet derivative is given by
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:deri}
    F_\varepsilon'(u) = \hat E_0^*\left(\int_0^T\nabla y\cdot \nabla p\,\mathrm{d}t\right)\,\Phi_\varepsilon'(u) \in L^1(\omega_c),
  \end{equation}
  where $y=y(\hat E\Phi_\varepsilon(u))$ is the solution of \eqref{eq:weak}, $p$ is the solution of \eqref{eq:adjoint}, and $\hat E_0^*:L^2(\Omega)\to L^2(\omega_c)$ is the restriction operator.

  If \cref{ass:data} holds, $F_\varepsilon'(u) \in L^{\frac{2q}{2+q}}(\omega_c)$ for the $q>2$ given in \cref{prop:state_regularity}.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:optimality}
  If $\varepsilon>0$ and \cref{ass:data} holds, every local minimizer $\bar u\in BV(\omega_c)$ to \eqref{eq:problem} satisfies
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:optimality}
    -F_\varepsilon'(\bar u)\in \alpha\,\partial G(\bar u) + \beta\,\partial \mathrm{TV}(\bar u)\subset L^\frac{2q}{2+q}(\omega_c),
  \end{equation}
  where $G$ and $\mathrm{TV}$ are considered as extended real-valued convex functionals on $L^\frac{2q}{q-2}(\omega_c)$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:optsys_pd}
  For any local minimizer $\bar u\in BV(\omega_c)$ to \eqref{eq:problem}, there exist $\bar q \in L^\frac{2q}{2+q}(\omega_c)$ and $\bar \xi \in L^{\frac{2q}{2+q}}(\omega_c)$ satisfying
  \begin{equation}\label{eq:optsys_pd}
    \left\{
      \begin{aligned}
        0 &= F_\varepsilon'(\bar u) + \alpha\bar q + \beta \bar \xi,\\
        \bar q &\in \partial G(\bar u),\\
        \bar \xi &\in \partial \mathrm{TV}(\bar u).
      \end{aligned}
    \right.
  \end{equation}
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
We call $y_{\vartheta}\in D_{\vartheta}:=D_h \otimes D_\tau$ a discrete solution of \eqref{eq:weak} if $y_{\vartheta}$ satisfies
  \begin{multline}\label{eq:discreteSolutdef}
    \int_0^T-(\partial_t y_{\vartheta},\partial_t v)_{H}-(\sigma -\tfrac16)\tau^2(\hat Eu_h\nabla \partial_t y_{\vartheta},\nabla \partial_tv)_{\mathbb{L}^2(\Omega)}+ (\hat Eu_h\nabla y_{\vartheta},\nabla v)_{\mathbb{L}^2(\Omega)}\,\mathrm{d}t\\
    = (y_1,v(0))_{H} + \int_0^T(f,v)_{H}\,\mathrm{d}t
  \end{multline}
  for all $v \in D_{\vartheta}$ with $v(T)=0$ and initial condition $y_{\vartheta}(0)=S_0 y_0$ defined via
  \begin{equation*}
    (S_0 y_0,\varphi)_{H}=(y_0,\varphi)_{H}\quad \forall\varphi \in D_h.
  \end{equation*}
<!-- end definition-1 -->
